decision: counted the surface before changing anything: 40 vitest files, about 9500 lines, 4 configs, 4 manifests
why: wanted the size and the violation census before a cross-cutting run
result: 52 mechanical violations, 248 review notes

decision: built a static checker for the mechanically decidable AGENTS.md rules instead of auditing by hand
why: the script is the artifact a reviewer reruns, and it makes every later check cheap
result: 12 rule detectors, runs in about 2s

decision: added a known-bad and a known-good fixture per rule because a silently broken detector reports zero violations
why: verify the gate before trusting a green result
result: selftest green; two detector bugs found and fixed (expect-chain pollution, resolves/rejects chain)

decision: added coverage.include and the v8 provider to both OAuth extensions
why: the rule requires completely untested source files to be visible

decision: replaced 23 manual process.env save and restore blocks with vi.stubEnv and vi.unstubAllEnvs, and moved FORCE_COLOR into the vitest config env
why: unmanaged global mutation leaks between tests; FORCE_COLOR has to exist before the module import
result: 29 env violations cleared, all four suites green

decision: replaced hand-rolled poll loops with vi.waitFor, shell settle sleeps with process-group death, and the dialog sleep with a held deferred
why: never wait on wall-clock time when a real state change can be observed
result: 12 real-wait violations cleared

decision: replaced the in-process descendant settle sleeps with a test-controlled pending-work gate
why: an aborted descendant has no observable death, so the test now releases the pending work itself and fails if the abort failed to cancel it
result: 3 sleeps removed

decision: deleted the abort-path clearPendingWork call and watched the two worker tests fail, then restored it
why: a passing assertion that cannot fail proves nothing
result: 2 tests failed as expected; reverted

decision: paired each absence-only assertion with the presence on the other input, and added a positive request assertion to the antigravity beta-header test
why: an assertion has to prove the behavior the test name claims
result: 6 weak assertions cleared, 105 tui-parity tests green

decision: fanned the file-by-file judgment audit out to six workers, each owning a disjoint file set under one written contract
why: bulk reading of 9500 lines would fill the main context
result: in progress

decision: wired the checker into npm run check:tests and the Makefile verify chain

result: gate runs on every verify

decision: six auditors reported; I reviewed every diff and kept only changes that preserve behavior
